title: Philippines misses crown bids in Miss Universe, Miss International
summary: It is a sad day for the Philippines as the delegates of the country in the Miss Universe and Miss International pageants failed to bag the crown.

blocks.text: November 26, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — It is a sad day for the Philippines as the delegates of the country in the Miss Universe and Miss International pageants failed to bag the crown.
Miss Universe candidate Bea Millan-Windorski was 3rd runner-up while Miss International bet Katrina Anne Johnson made it to the Top 20.
Home court candidate Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico won the Miss Universe crown after three hours of competition.
Barreto bested 115 queens with Melissa Núñez of Dominican Republic as 1st runner-up and Clara Vegas of Venezuela as 2nd runner-up.
Bea entered the Top 30 as one of two Asians, along with Kaziah Liz Mejo of India, to make the first cut.
Several Asian delegates were not able to compete this year due to franchise or licensing disputes or withdrawal due to various reasons.
Her flawless pasarela was worthy enough to earn her spot in the Top 12, making her the only Asian candidate still gunning for the crown.
Bea looked ethereal during the evening gown competition with her gown in the color of the “Pearl of the Orient” designed by Anthony Ramirez.
This earned her a spot in the Top 5 and was asked during the Q&A portion: “After 75 years, how will you convince doubters that the Miss Universe pageant is still relevant?”
Bea stressed the need to pass on the wisdom that she learned from the past generation to the future of the world.

“And I would use their wisdom to guide the present so that we could build the kind of future that we all deserve. I would use my experience in the international arena to work with the United Nations to continue my work advocating for climate displaced communities and vulnerable places all around the world,” she added.
In the Final Q&A, Bea emphasized the need for world leaders to listen when asked: “What does the world need most from its leaders right now?”

“As someone who has been an environmentalist my whole life, I wish that our leaders would listen to nature and realize that they have much to learn. I volunteered with sea turtles for the past 10 years and while we’ve often heard of the crab mentality or tearing one another down, the turtle mentality is the opposite,” the beauty queen said.

“The strongest sea turtle hatchlings actually stay behind in the nest to help their weaker brothers and sisters out and into the sea. I wish that our world leaders would embrace the same mentality and realize that when one rises, we all rise,” she added.
After Georgia Waddington of New Zealand was called as 4th runner-up, Bea was called next, giving the Philippines a second consecutive year in the runners-up circle.
Last year, the Philippines’ Ahtisa Manalo also ended her journey as 3rd runner-up, with Mexico’s Fátima Bosch winning the crown.
Bea was aiming to be the Philippines’ fifth Miss Universe titleholder after Catriona Gray (2018), Pia Wurtzbach (2015), Margie Moran (1973) and Gloria Diaz (1969).
In a Facebook post after the pageant ceremony, Windorski said she fought for the country until the very end.
Meanwhile, Johnson has ended her journey in the Miss International 2026 competition in the Top 20, out of more than 70 contestants overall at the competition in Tokyo.
Katrina was at the top of her game with her blue skirt sportswear, which replaces the swimsuit round.
The Filipina queen looked angelic in her white and gold gown and made it to the semifinals, entering the Top 20.
Unfortunately, Katrina failed to enter the Top 10 and the Sustainable Development Goals speech round.
Katrina continued the semifinal streak of the Philippines after Myrna Esguerra was 4th runner-up.
She was aiming for the country’s seventh Miss International crown which was last won in 2016 by Kylie Versoza.
